subject: Renewal: Quantify Health — tier rebalancing & upside rebate proposal
messages:
From: Megan Park <megan@quantifyhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing discussion — Quantify Health

Hi Jasmine,

Our leadership is starting the renewal conversations and asked for an updated view of pricing if we: 1) shift 40% of current burst volume into a committed tier, and 2) add a short-term safety floor for the next 6 months while we finish a cost-optimization project.

Specifically, we want to understand:
- What a blended unit price looks like with a 12-month term and the 40% committed shift
- Whether Redwood can provide a temporary "usage floor" credit if we dip below commit during the optimization period
- Any upside rebate mechanics if we exceed commitments by 25%+ in a quarter

I attached our Q1 usage snapshot so you have the numbers. Can we get a proposal by next Wednesday? We have procurement on a hard deadline of 3/8.

Thanks,
Megan Park
Head of Platform, Quantify Health
[Attachment: QH_usage_report_Q1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Park <megan@quantifyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing discussion — Quantify Health

Hi Megan,

Thanks — received the usage snapshot and sharing internally. Appreciate the clarity on timelines. We'll put together two options:

Option A (Predictable): 12mo committed tier covering 40% of current burst volume + a 6-month usage-floor credit that smooths to the commit if usage falls below the floor. This keeps unit price predictable and gives you runway while you optimize.

Option B (Flexible + Upside): 12mo smaller commit (25%) with a rolling rebate trigger: if you exceed the commit by 25%+ in any quarter, you receive an embedded rebate that scales with overage bands (tiered). This reduces upfront financial exposure and shares upside.

I'll draft proposed terms and loop Ben to review SLAs and commercial flexibility. Can you confirm whether procurement prefers credits applied as invoice credits or prepaid retainers (they noted both are possible)?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal pricing discussion — Quantify Health

Jasmine / Monica —

Quick notes after skimming the usage file: peak 95th pct traffic spikes are concentrated in a two-week window each month; good candidate for a mixed commit + burst overlay.

Commercially I'd propose the following structure to balance risk:
- Baseline commit: 35% of average monthly consumption (12-mo term) at a 12% unit discount vs list.
- Safety floor credit: if monthly usage < 60% of committed level, Redwood issues a pro-rated invoice credit up to 3 months (ceiling = 10% of monthly commit spend).
- Upside rebate: for quarterly usage > 125% of commit for that quarter, apply a rebate equal to 6% of incremental spend above 125% (capped at 15% of quarterly spend). Rebate issued as invoice credit the following invoice.

Two asks for Jasmine: 1) confirm the numbers against Q1 snapshot and model blended unit price for procurement, 2) prepare a short one-pager (proposed_terms_QH_v2.pdf) that frames the move and shows sample math for a typical month and for a spike month.

Ben
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Park <megan@quantifyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Quantify Health — tier rebalancing & upside rebate proposal

Hi Megan — attaching the proposed terms and a sample month calc per Ben's guidance. Quick summary up front:

- Recommended: Baseline commit = 35% of avg monthly usage (12mo) at 12% discount vs list; 6-month safety-floor credit that covers up to 10% of monthly commit spend (applied as invoice credit).
- Upside rebate: quarterly overage band starting at 125% of commit with a 6% rebate on incremental spend (rebate credited next invoice, cap = 15% of quarter spend).
- SLA note: if average p95 latency in any month exceeds our SLA, customer can request a remediation credit; separate clause in appendix.

Attachments: proposed_terms_QH_v2.pdf (one-pager with sample math) and QH_usage_report_Q1.xlsx you originally shared.

Next steps: if this looks directionally acceptable, I can convert the terms into a short amendment and route to procurement; if procurement prefers a prepaid retainer instead of invoice credits we can update the flow in the amendment.

Would you like a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the sample math?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
